# Organisation and Authority
## Corporate Security General site security, responsible for the site, its staff and its property. Officers rank up by time in post. - [bold]WY-SEC-TCSO Trainee Corporate Security Officer[/bold] (TCSO.): probationary officer. Patrols with an Officer or above. - [bold]WY-SEC Corporate Security Officer[/bold] (Off.): officer. - [bold]WY-SEC-SPEC Senior Corporate Security Officer[/bold] (Sr. Off.): experienced officer. Leads patrols and supervises trainees. - [bold]WY-SEC-LEAD Corporate Security Sergeant[/bold] (CSSgt.): head of site security. Assigns officers, runs the armoury and commands the guard detail.
## Personal Protection Close protection for Company executives. Personal Protection answers to its Coordinator, and through them to the executive it protects. - [bold]WY-SEC-TPPO Trainee Personal Protection Officer[/bold] (TPPO.) - [bold]WY-SEC-PPO Personal Protection Officer[/bold] (PPO.) - [bold]WY-SEC-PPS Personal Protection Specialist[/bold] (PPS.): the detail's heavy weapon. - [bold]WY-SEC-PPC Personal Protection Coordinator[/bold] (PPC.): leads the detail and decides where its executives may safely go.
## Chain of Command - The Security Sergeant commands Corporate Security and reports to the senior Company employee on site. - The senior employee on site is normally the [bold]Corporate Liaison[/bold]. Any Company employee of grade [bold]WYC7 or above[/bold] outranks the Liaison while present. - Personal Protection takes its orders from its Coordinator. The Coordinator takes them from the executive the detail protects. - In an emergency, Corporate Security may give orders to any office or research employee for their safety. Those orders are to be followed. - Security doesn't take orders from colonial officials, the colony's marshals or any outside force.
## Armoury - The armoury is held by the Security Sergeant. - Weapons beyond an officer's issued kit are signed out by the Sergeant and returned at the end of the incident. - Officers may not arm office or research staff.
